messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

I’d be happiest with a dependable, simpler setup that needs little cleaning or upkeep; after long days, I’d rather not have coffee turn into another task. The leak is the main thing I’ve noticed. I can’t think of a separate grinder issue, though I may be missing something. I’d also need to be careful not to take on repairs or a cleaning rota.

I want the old machine repaired and kept, because it matters to me—it was my dad’s. But it keeps breaking, and the leak and ongoing fuss are a pain; I don’t have much spare time to deal with it. The grinder’s fine as far as I can tell. Nothing’s settled yet.

I just want the kitchen coffee working again without this turning into a bigger conflict. The leak is a problem, but I don’t want to take sides or manage the repair. I’m tired, so I can’t take on chasing everyone about it.
Not quite. “Keep something” is too vague—I mean keep the old machine running. The rest fits.
Both matter, but I want it repaired and used—not just displayed. Keeping Dad’s machine running is part of keeping that connection. I also need it not to keep draining my time.
Yes, that fits. Mark it confirmed.

I do have a small concern: these all keep the old machine as the main setup, so they don’t really address my preference for something simpler. And “whoever uses it” wiping it could become an unclear ongoing expectation. I’d rather not be responsible for organizing or chasing maintenance.

Option 3 is closest to what I want. My concern with option 1 is that “whoever uses it” could turn cleaning into another chore. Option 2’s extra setup may also need upkeep. Costs and who books service still need sorting.
No strong discomfort with the options. I’d just want to be clear that I’m not the one booking service or chasing it; I can’t take that on.

#4 is closer to what I’d hope for, though keeping two machines could add complexity, and I’d want cleaning clearly covered without becoming my responsibility. #4 and #5 fit as statements of my concerns; I’m not comfortable with option 5’s wipe-after-use expectation for me.

#6 mostly fits, but “never” is too absolute. I want cleaning and servicing arrangements clear up front so they don’t become my chore. Option 5 is closer; option 4 means maintaining two machines, which sounds like more hassle.
#7 fits. I don’t have a strong discomfort with either option, as long as booking and chasing service genuinely sit with office/facilities—not me.
